trials.summary: Trial 01 (sw=0.409, h_f=1.837, h_s=3.354, cap=0.156): objective 0.1243 +/- 0.0809 above the exp5 honest level; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite on all 8 (mu rel-RMSE 58.1%, gamma rel-RMSE 27.3%).
trials.key_insight: Moderate sigma damping (sw 0.41) + flat sigma kernel (h_s 3.35) keeps gamma finite and divergence-free, but mu stays strongly biased, so the score design alone does not yet beat the frozen exp5 level.

trials.summary: Trial 02 (sw=0.884, h_f=0.642, h_s=1.007, cap=0.054): objective 0.1287 +/- 0.0844, 0 diverged cells, gamma finite; gamma rel-RMSE 17.0% but mu blew up at low T (rel-RMSE 95.9%), worse than trial_01.
trials.key_insight: Near-exp5 sigma settings with a sharpened FWHM kernel (h_f 0.64) worsen the low-T mu overshoot (mu rel-RMSE 95.9%) while improving gamma (17.0%); low-T mu accuracy, not sigma damping alone, is the binding problem.

trials.summary: Trial 03 (sw=0.956, h_f=2.450, h_s=3.017, cap=0.215): objective 0.1040 +/- 0.0582 - new best, below the exp5 honest level and the 0.1074 headline; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite on all 8 (mu rel-RMSE 45.8%, gamma rel-RMSE 23.3%).
trials.key_insight: Restoring near-full sigma weight (sw 0.96) while keeping both kernels flat (h_f 2.45, h_s 3.02) beats the exp5 level at 0.1040, so the flat-kernel score design rather than sigma damping carries the improvement.

trials.summary: Trial 04 (sw=0.959, h_f=2.101, h_s=2.126, cap=0.249): objective 0.1177 +/- 0.0687 - second best, worse than trial_03; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 50.4%, gamma rel-RMSE 28.9%).
trials.key_insight: Sharpening both KDE kernels (h_f 2.45->2.10, h_s 3.02->2.13) from the best point raised the objective 0.1040->0.1177, so kernel flatness rather than the sigma weight drives trial_03 advantage.

trials.summary: Trial 05 (sw=0.844, h_f=3.903, h_s=3.616, cap=0.217): objective 0.0822 +/- 0.0244 - new best by a wide margin, well below the exp5 level and the 0.1074 headline; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 36.7%, gamma rel-RMSE 21.0%).
trials.key_insight: Pushing both KDE kernels toward their upper bounds (h_f 3.90, h_s 3.62) with a strong sigma link gave the best result yet (0.0822), confirming kernel flatness as the dominant lever over the sigma weight.

trials.summary: Trial 06 (sw=0.497, h_f=4.0, h_s=3.876, cap=0.104): objective 0.0861 +/- 0.0247 - second best, just above trial_05; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 34.0% best, gamma rel-RMSE 30.1% worse).
trials.key_insight: Maximally flat kernels with a moderate sigma weight (sw 0.50) matched but did not beat trial_05; the lower sw and smaller gamma cap raised the gamma error (30.1% vs 21.0%), so the best region needs a strong sigma weight together with flat kernels.

trials.summary: Trial 07 (sw=0.865, h_f=4.0, h_s=3.675, cap=0.107): objective 0.0803 +/- 0.0239 - new best, marginally over trial_05; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 35.9%, gamma rel-RMSE 22.3%).
trials.key_insight: Combining trial_05 strong sigma weight (0.865) with trial_06 max-flat kernels (h_f 4.0, h_s 3.68) gave the new best 0.0803, so the two design choices are complementary rather than redundant.

trials.summary: Trial 08 (sw=0.869, h_f=3.985, h_s=3.624, cap=0.295): objective 0.0876 +/- 0.0238 - worse than trial_07; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 37.0%, gamma rel-RMSE 24.6%).
trials.key_insight: In the best kernel/sigma region, a larger gamma cap (0.295 vs trial_07 0.107) worsened the objective (0.0876 vs 0.0803), so a small gamma trust region is preferred.

trials.summary: Trial 09 (sw=0.847, h_f=4.0, h_s=3.603, cap=0.231): objective 0.0839 +/- 0.0252 - third best; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 35.5%, gamma rel-RMSE 27.9%).
trials.key_insight: A larger gamma cap (0.231) again raised the gamma error (27.9% vs trial_07 22.3% at cap 0.107), reinforcing that a small gamma trust region is best in the optimum region.

trials.summary: Trial 10 (sw=0.832, h_f=3.864, h_s=3.673, cap=0.083): objective 0.0922 +/- 0.0268 - worse than trial_07; 0 diverged cells, gamma finite (mu rel-RMSE 37.6%, gamma rel-RMSE 26.9%).
trials.key_insight: A smaller gamma cap (0.083) also worsened the objective relative to trial_07 (0.107), so the gamma-cap optimum is a narrow band near ~0.1-0.15 rather than either extreme.

protocol.model: series-21 (17g) model on REAL data; mu reward = Anuar's per-run likelihood (MU_REWARD=loglik_mean), mu score denominator = per-experiment sigma_prop (MU_SCORE=sigma_prop)
protocol.question: experiment_6 - score-DESIGN campaign for failure mode #8: the learning-rate schedule is FROZEN to the experiment_5 winner (trial_21) and the campaign tunes the sigma_fit KDE channel (damping + bandwidths) and a relative gamma trust region.

frozen_schedule.note: experiment_5 winning trial (trial_21); the schedule is a plateau and is NOT searched here

protocol.no_clipping: CLIP = inf AND parameter clamps removed (mu/gamma unbounded)

divergence_guard.note: STOP the experiment and record diverged/diverged_at if a parameter leaves this band (guards the photon-count blow-up)

protocol.objective: T-weighted mean of CAP-capped per-cell rel-sq errors; err_i = min(rel_sq_i, CAP=1.0); w(T) = 0.25 + 0.75*T/100; objective = sum(w*err)/sum(w)
frozen: Anuar's mu reward (loglik_mean) + sigma_prop score denominator
tunable: gamma_rel_cap float  0.0 .. 0.5   (per-step relative gamma trust region; 0=off)
protocol.success_bar: beat the experiment_5 honest level (objective ~0.108-0.113, best 0.1074) on the same T-weighted capped metric, with gamma finite on all 8 cells and fewer/zero diverged cells
